notes: Before anything starts, Nodeau can now show you where a model would run, what it would cost and why. Run nodeau run with --explain, or press Preview in app.nodeau.ai, and you get the machine and accelerator Nodeau would choose across your fleet, the memory the model is expected to need, what is available right now, how much Nodeau keeps back for your system and whether that figure was measured on your machine or is Nodeau's conservative default, and every other machine's reason. Every number says where it came from: measured, estimated, observed right now or Nodeau's own policy. The safety reserve now has two parts: a floor that is never given away, and a margin above it that you can set aside for one run on the one machine you were shown, with the new arithmetic in front of you before you agree. When the hardware itself is too small, no override is offered. New: nodeau benchmark measures how much memory this machine needs to keep for itself, and a Mac can measure a model's own footprint. Nothing changes until you adopt the result with nodeau benchmark adopt, and nodeau benchmark reset puts the conservative default back. A calibration lasts 30 days and is set aside by itself when the operating system, the hardware or the driver changes, and nodeau doctor tells you which reserve each machine is using. On Linux a card's figure is the whole card's, and Nodeau says so. This release also includes everything in v0.18.0-beta.5.
